title: Copying and Immutability knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the main idea of “Copying and Immutability”?
options: It means all Kotlin libraries and platform APIs behave identically.
It removes the need to understand types or runtime behavior.
Apply copying and immutability by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail.
It makes versioning, input validation, and testing unnecessary.
questions.answer_key: Apply copying and immutability by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail.
questions.explanation: The reliable answer is grounded in the lesson’s main principle: Apply copying and immutability by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which learning/debugging practice is most reliable for “Copying and Immutability”?
options: Assume the compiler or toolchain is broken without reducing the example.
Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
Change several unrelated parts at once and keep the result that looks plausible.
Ignore warnings and suppress failures before identifying the cause.
questions.answer_key: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A minimal reproducible example and version-aware testing separate a real behavior from a mistaken assumption. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which claim should a learner avoid when applying “Copying and Immutability”?
options: A data class copy recursively duplicates every object referenced by its properties.
Never inspect the official API reference for the selected target.
Treat draft or experimental features as universally stable.
Expose every internal implementation detail to every caller.
questions.answer_key: A data class copy recursively duplicates every object referenced by its properties.
questions.explanation: The misconception to avoid is: A data class copy recursively duplicates every object referenced by its properties. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.
